Redis-backed session cookies are explicitly configured with httponly=False, making the authentication session identifier readable by JavaScript. This enables session theft when an XSS payload executes.
Successful login adds user_id to the existing session without invalidating or rotating its identifier. A party that knows a pre-login session identifier can reuse it after the victim authenticates.
Passwords are verified using unsalted MD5. MD5 is a fast, obsolete hash unsuitable for password storage, enabling efficient offline cracking of database hashes.
